Recovering Weather-Station Latitude (PS1 → PS2)¶

Problem. For 2020–21 data, latitude was corrupted to -9999. PS1 (2000–2020) has known latitudes for stations in Brazil's North region; PS2 (2020–21) does not, and some PS2 sensors may be new and outside that region.

Goals. (1) Predict the latitude of every PS2 sensor. (2) Identify which PS2 sensors are not part of PS1.

This notebook tells the story step by step using the latpred package in src/. The same steps run headless with python -m latpred.pipeline (or make run / ./run.sh). Every figure is also saved to reports/figures/.

Executive summary¶

Findings

  • Of 35 PS2 sensors, 22 are re-identified as continuing PS1 stations; 11 are not part of PS1 (8 new stations inside the North region, 3 well outside it); 2 have no usable data. The three out-of-region sensors sit at roughly -16°, -28° and -31°: central-west and southern Brazil, 12–27° south of the southernmost PS1 station. One of them has July mean temperatures near 16 °C, a climate absent from PS1.
  • Learned model: gradient boosting on station-month climate features predicts the latitude of a never-seen PS1 station with MAE 1.14° (leave-one-station-out). That is a 27% improvement over predicting the mean (1.56°). Random Forest reached 1.25° and Ridge 1.40°.
  • Tree models cannot extrapolate. Trained on stations at or below 1°N, the model placed stations at 2.8°–4.5°N between -0.9° and -2.7°. A model trained only on PS1 cannot locate southern stations on its own.
  • Physics estimator fills the gap. Inverting the clear-sky solar geometry from each sensor's radiation profile recovers PS1 latitude with MAE 1.6° and longitude with MAE 1.0°, with no latitude training. It is used for out-of-region sensors, where its signal is strongest.
  • Re-identification of a station across years works 85% of the time (top-1 on PS1 2016–18 → 2019). The calibrated threshold accepts 78% of true matches and rejects 74% of simulated new stations. In a simulated end-to-end test the full decision rule gives MAE 0.31° for continuing stations and 1.09° for new in-region stations.

Recommendations

  1. Treat out-of-region predictions as approximate (±3–5°) and the matched-station predictions as reliable. Prioritise the 11 non-PS1 sensors for metadata recovery.
  2. The largest lift would come from training data outside the North region: INMET's national station list or ERA5 reanalysis. That turns extrapolation into interpolation.
  3. Fix the data pipeline at source. Every metadata column in PS2 is corrupted, not only latitude, and station codes in PS1 are inconsistent (e.g. one site appears under two codes).

Approach¶

Step What Why
1. Audit & clean Convert -9999 and physically impossible values to NaN Sentinels would otherwise dominate every statistic
2. Define stations Cluster PS1 files by location (≤0.1°) into 43 physical stations Each station spans 2–3 files and station codes are inconsistent; grouping prevents leakage in validation
3. Station-month features Climate levels, diurnal harmonics, pressure tides, wind vector, radiation-profile shape, month as sin/cos PS2 sensors have 1–16 usable months; the station prediction is the median over its months
4. Learned model Baseline vs Ridge vs Random Forest vs Gradient Boosting, leave-one-station-out CV The honest question is accuracy on a station the model has never seen
5. Physics model Invert clear-sky solar geometry from the radiation profile Trees cannot extrapolate beyond PS1's -3.9° to 4.5°; the sun's geometry has no training range
6. In PS1? Fingerprint re-identification (calibrated on PS1), kNN climate novelty, physics consistency Separates known stations, new in-region stations and new out-of-region stations
7. Decision rule Out of region → physics; re-identified → known latitude; otherwise → ML Each estimator is used where its validation says it works

1. Preprocessing: load, clean and audit¶

Cleaning rules live in latpred/config.py (VALID_RANGE) and latpred/preprocessing.py.

In [2]:
ps1 = preprocessing.assign_station_ids(preprocessing.load_folder(paths.data_dir / "ps1"))
ps2 = preprocessing.load_folder(paths.data_dir / "ps2")
coords = preprocessing.station_coordinates(ps1)
preprocessing.audit_table(ps1, ps2)

Observations

  • Readings are every 4 hours (00, 04, …, 20 UTC). Radiation is not reported at night, so ~55% of radiation values are missing even in PS1.
  • PS1 covers only Brazil's North region (AM, PA, AP, RR), so latitudes run from -3.9° to 4.5°.
  • In PS2 every location field (region, state, station, longitude, height) is corrupted, not only latitude.
In [3]:
miss = preprocessing.missingness(ps1, ps2)
display(viz.plot_missingness(miss, FIG))
display(viz.plot_ps2_coverage(ps2, FIG))

Missing-data strategy. Raw hourly values are not imputed. A month is used only if it has ≥60 valid 4-hourly temperature readings (~10 days). Within a usable month, features can still be NaN (e.g. no radiation sensor). Gradient boosting handles NaN natively; Ridge and RF impute medians inside the CV pipeline. Sensors with no usable month fall back to the physics estimate, or are flagged.

2. Feature engineering (station-month)¶

  • Temperature, dew point, humidity levels and diurnal amplitude: continental vs coastal climates.
  • Season: month as sin/cos, so the model can relate seasonal behaviour to hemisphere.
  • Wind vector (u, v): trade winds blow from the NE north of the ITCZ and from the SE south of it.
  • Pressure tides (S1/S2): the semidiurnal tide amplitude falls roughly as cos³(latitude). Absolute pressure is excluded from the regressor because it mostly encodes elevation.
  • Radiation-profile shape: morning/afternoon radiation relative to midday, at fixed UTC hours, encodes day length and solar time.

At least one PS2 sensor drops to ~16 °C in July, colder than any PS1 station: a subtropical, southern-hemisphere station, well outside the PS1 region. Individually, no single feature correlates strongly with latitude inside PS1's narrow band, so the model must combine weak signals.

3. Modeling: leave-one-station-out comparison¶

Each fold holds out all months of one physical station; the station prediction is the median of its monthly predictions.

4. Evaluation: can the learned model extrapolate?¶

Train on stations at or below 2° and predict the three northernmost (2.8°–4.5°), mimicking PS2 sensors outside the training range.

In [9]:

display(ext.round(2))
display(viz.plot_extrapolation(ext, FIG))
true_lat ml_pred max_train_lat
station_id
STN20 3.81 -1.68 0.95
STN21 2.82 -2.72 0.95
STN29 4.48 -0.87 0.95

The tree model cannot predict beyond the latitudes it was trained on. For sensors far outside the North region we need an estimator that does not depend on the training range.

5. Physics model: inverting the sun's geometry¶

For each sensor, the 90th-percentile radiation per (month, UTC hour) approximates clear sky. A grid search finds the latitude, longitude and transmissivity k that best fit the theoretical clear-sky radiation over the same accumulation hour (declination and equation of time: Spencer 1971; clear-sky: Haurwitz 1945). Quality gates (k in [0.6, 1.2], RMSE < 250 kJ/m²) are the only tuned parts.

In [10]:
phys1 = physics.physics_table(ps1, "station_id")
phys2 = physics.physics_table(ps2, "file")
phys_eval = physics.evaluate_physics(phys1, coords)
display(pd.Series(phys_eval).round(2).to_frame("PS1 physics validation"))
display(viz.plot_physics_validation(phys1, coords, FIG))
PS1 physics validation
n_valid 31.00
n_total 43.00
lat_mae 1.64
lat_p90 3.87
lat_bias 0.54
lon_mae 1.02

Inside the narrow PS1 band the physics estimate is less precise than the learned model: near the equator the sun's seasonal cycle barely changes with latitude, and Amazon cloud seasonality biases the clear-sky proxy. Its value is that it has no training range, and its latitude signal grows quickly away from the equator. Recovering longitude to ~1° confirms the method is physically sound.

6. Which PS2 sensors are already in PS1?¶

6a. Re-identification¶

PS1 ends 2020-01-01 and PS2 starts 2020-01-02, so many PS2 sensors are probably the same stations. The fingerprint (absolute pressure ≈ elevation, temperature, dew point, humidity, diurnal amplitude and phase, wind, radiation shape) is compared calendar month by calendar month. The threshold is calibrated on PS1: 2019 data as the query, 2016–2018 data as the reference.

In [11]:
scale = matching.fingerprint_scale(f1)
cal = matching.calibrate_matching(f1, scale)
print(f"{len(cal.d_true)} PS1 stations have both periods. Top-1 re-identification accuracy: {cal.top1.mean():.0%}")
print(f"Threshold {cal.threshold:.2f}: re-identifies {cal.recall:.0%} of known stations, "
      f"rejects {cal.reject:.0%} of simulated new stations (balanced accuracy {cal.balanced_accuracy:.0%})")
display(viz.plot_matching_calibration(cal, FIG))

27 PS1 stations have both periods. Top-1 re-identification accuracy: 85%
Threshold 0.53: re-identifies 78% of known stations, rejects 74% of simulated new stations (balanced accuracy 76%)

6b. Climate novelty¶

Each station-month is compared with its 5 nearest PS1 station-months. The reference distribution scores every PS1 station against the other PS1 stations; anything above the maximum has a climate unlike any North-region station.

In [12]:
nov = matching.NoveltyScorer().fit(f1)
nov2 = nov.score(f2, "file")
print(f"PS1 leave-one-out novelty: median {nov.null_.median():.2f}, max {nov.threshold_:.2f} (threshold). "
      f"PS2 sensors above: {(nov2 > nov.threshold_).sum()} of {len(nov2)}")
display(viz.plot_novelty(nov.null_, nov2, nov.threshold_, FIG))

PS1 leave-one-out novelty: median 1.95, max 5.96 (threshold). PS2 sensors above: 1 of 33

7. Simulated end-to-end validation on PS1¶

The decision rule is replayed on PS1 2019 data in two scenarios: known station (its older data is in the reference pool) and new station (removed, so any match is a false match). ML predictions are leave-one-station-out.

In [13]:
sim, sim_summary = evaluation.simulate_decision_rule(cal, oof[best].pred, coords.lat)
display(sim_summary.round(2))
display(viz.plot_simulation(sim_summary, FIG))
MAE median_AE share_matched ML-only MAE
scenario
known station 0.31 0.00 0.81 1.04
new station 1.09 0.67 0.26 1.04

For a continuing station, re-identification brings the error well below ML alone. For a genuinely new station, a false match costs little versus pure ML because neighbouring stations have similar latitudes.

8. PS2 predictions¶

Decision rule (latpred/decision.py):

  1. Out of region: novelty above every PS1 station, or a quality-checked physics latitude more than the physics 90th-percentile error outside the PS1 band → physics latitude.
  2. Known PS1 station: fingerprint distance below the threshold (one-to-one Hungarian assignment), not out of region, not contradicted by physics → that station's latitude.
  3. New station in region → ML latitude.
  4. No usable data → PS1 mean, flagged.
In [14]:
res = pd.DataFrame(index=pd.Index(sorted(ps2.file.unique()), name="file"))
res = (res.join(modeling.predict_stations(model, f2, "file"))
          .join(phys2[["phys_lat", "phys_lon", "phys_k", "phys_rmse", "phys_ok"]])
          .join(matching.match_sensors(f1, f2, scale)))
res["novelty"] = nov2
res = decision.apply_decision_rule(res, coords=coords, match_th=cal.threshold,
                                   novelty_th=nov.threshold_, phys_p90=phys_eval["lat_p90"])
pred = decision.to_output_table(res)
pred.to_csv(paths.output_dir / "prediction_results.csv", index=False)
print(pred.status.value_counts().to_string())

9. Assumptions, limitations and next steps¶

Assumptions and their consequences

  • Climate is stable between PS1 (≤2019) and PS2 (2020–21). A sensor swap or recalibration makes a known station look new, sending it to the ML estimate: less accurate, not catastrophic.
  • UTC timestamps; radiation accumulated over the previous hour. Supported by the physics fit recovering longitude to ~1°.
  • The 90th-percentile radiation approximates clear sky. This is weakest in the cloudy Amazon wet season, the main source of physics error near the equator.

Expected accuracy on PS2: known stations ≈ the simulated 0.3° MAE; new in-region stations ≈ 1.1°; out-of-region stations ≈ ±3–5° (physics), which cannot be verified with North-only training data.

Next steps (expected lift)

  1. Add public station metadata (INMET) or ERA5 reanalysis covering all of Brazil. This turns extrapolation into interpolation and is the largest lift: likely ±1° nationwide.
  2. Cross-correlate daily weather anomalies with nearby known stations over overlapping periods, for near-exact re-identification.
  3. A turbidity-aware clear-sky model (e.g. pvlib Ineichen-Perez) and day-level clear-sky detection to reduce physics error in the tropics.
  4. Joint latitude/longitude modelling to remove the UTC-hour/longitude confounding in the ML features.
  5. Conformal prediction intervals from the leave-one-station-out residuals.

An AI assistant (Anthropic's Claude) was used to draft the code, the notebook text and the Docker/bash scaffolding, under my direction. I reviewed the modelling choices, validation design and results, and the design decisions (station-month unit, leave-one-station-out validation, physics-based extrapolation, re-identification calibrated on PS1) are documented in this notebook so they can be checked and reproduced. If this work is shared as an interview submission, the summary and findings should be rewritten in the author's own words, per that challenge's guidance.
